zscape.name: ZSCAPE
zscape.kicker: Zebrafish Single-Cell Atlas of Perturbed Embryos
zscape.lede: Whole-embryo reverse genetics at single-cell resolution. Embryos are resolved individually, so cell-type abundance variance can be estimated first and perturbation effects measured against that baseline rather than against an assumed constant.

paper.citation: Saunders, Srivatsan, Duran, Dorrity, Ewing, Linbo, Shendure, Raible, Moens, Kimelman & Trapnell
paper.title: Embryo-scale reverse genetics at single-cell resolution

sections.title: Experimental design

rows.v: 1,812 individually resolved embryos, ≥8 per condition. Perturbation arm alone: 804 barcoded embryos over 98 conditions, 2.7 M cells in a single run.
18 → 96 hpf, reared at 28 °C. Four experiments: three wild-type time series plus the perturbation experiment.
Paper states 19; released metadata resolves 18 numeric values plus one blank level.
≈10% of cells per embryo; embryo-of-origin recovered for ≈70% of QC-passing cells via hashing.
1.24 M cells — wild-type time series plus ~600,000 control-injected cells, which showed no batch effect and were merged in.

sections.note: 28 released labels resolve to 23 distinct perturbations: the five null lines target five genes already perturbed as crispants. Confirmed by the authors' supplementary table, which pairs each as “gene” / “gene null”.

rows.v: sci-RNA-seq3 — combinatorial indexing on PFA-fixed nuclei (single-nucleus capture).
sci-Plex oligo hashing, one barcode per embryo.
Illumina NextSeq 500 / NextSeq 2000 / NovaSeq 6000.

sections.title: Provenance & caveats
bullets: The Lawson Lab annotation was tested directly and ruled out — 4.54% coordinate agreement, bidirectional deltas, and 3,629 ZSCAPE gene IDs absent from it entirely. It is a closed negative result, not an open alternative.
951 genes carry zero counts across all 1.24 M reference cells and were retained, confirming the 32,031-gene set is the reference itself rather than an expression filter.
The gene space contains no pseudogenes and no IG/TR segments — absence of such a gene is a property of the reference, not biological evidence.
num_cells_expressed in the gene metadata runs systematically higher than the matrix supports (median ratio 1.0076, never lower). Recompute from the matrix if the number matters.
The paper's only GRCz11/Ensembl sentence concerns harmonising other atlases for a cross-atlas comparison — it is not evidence about the counting reference.

sections.title: Provenance & caveats
bullets: The shared reference with ZSCAPE is the strongest cross-dataset fact we have: the two feature universes are identical gene-for-gene and position-for-position, so counts are directly comparable without gene-ID mapping.

Two QC discrepancies between the paper and the released object remain open — CHEM11's missing hash filtering and the absent round-1 80-UMI cells. Do not infer the missing cells from the filtered object; the pre-QC data is not available.
The published and reference columns are False for all 2,068,668 cells; meaning unclear.

The pectoral-fin subset carries genetic perturbations (hgfa-negsib, met-negsib, noto-negsib, mafba-negsib) on the same four genes as ZSCAPE's stable null lines — a direct experimental link between the two datasets.
BPCells files carry an 8-byte type header; reading from offset 0 silently corrupts every value. The CDS also needs monocle3 for S4 dispatch — without it, reach in via attr() only.
